recipes.name: Grandma's Slow Cooker Vegetarian Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 (15 ounce) can garbanzo beans, rinsed and drained
1 (14.5 ounce) can chopped tomatoes in puree
1 (15 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained
1 tablespoon chili powder, or to taste

steps.text: Combine black bean soup, kidney beans, garbanzo beans, baked beans, tomatoes, corn, onion, bell pepper, and celery. Season with garlic, chili powder, parsley, oregano, and basil.
Cook on High for at least 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma's Slow Cooker Vegetarian Chili
raw_recipe.description: Try this slow cooker vegetarian chili and you have a party in the making. The ingredients blend perfectly for a wonderful dish made easy in one pot.

video.description: Put your slow cooker to work making you a spectacular chili—simply throw in all of the ingredients and in 2 hours on high you've got yourself a warming, comforting meal for a crowd. Or put all the ingredients on low for dinner that's ready when you're home from work! Each bowl is highly receptive to sour cream and good, crusty bread.

review.reviewBody:
This is GREAT!!!! I made a BIG BATCH, so that I could freeze some!!! Here is what I used: 
1 - 40 1/2 oz kidney beans, rinsed and drained
2 - 16 oz great northern white, " "
2 - 16 oz black beans, " "
2 - 16 oz vegetarian baked beans - not drained
1 - 28 oz chunky crushed tomatoes in puree - " "
1 - 10oz rotel tomatoes, not drained
1 - 16oz frozen white sweet corn
I eliminated the celery, used the onion and garlic, and one green pepper, and added WAHOO Chili seasoning from Tastefully Simple, and some crushed red pepper. Did mine on low for 9 hours and it is GREAT!!!!!!!!! We are having some nice bread w/ it and putting some lowfat cheese and low fat sour cream on top!!!! YUM Great for a snowy day here in PA!!!!! Thank you Kevin....I like this chili w/o meat better than my usual w/ meat!!!!!!!!! This is a keeper!!!!!

This is one of my favorite recipes, although I tweek it quite a bit. For the seasoning, I always axe the oregano and add a chili mix in place of chili powder. I always double or triple the tomatoes, using a variety of crushed, diced, puree, and whole tomatoes. I found a small can of black bean soup in the goya aisle (in case anyone was still searching for black bean soup).

I wasn’t sure how to rate this, but decided on 5 stars because if it weren’t for this recipe and the reviews from others I would not have found my all-time favorite vegetarian recipe. I kept the bean combination (shout out to the reviewer who said the black bean soup can be found in the Hispanic aisle made by Goya) andI literally nixed the rest of the recipe. Instead, into the crock pot I added the beans, 28 oz can crushed tomatoes, 14.5 oz diced tomatoes, 1 cup water or vegetable broth, 3 tbsp of Chili powder, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 - 2 chilis in adobo finely diced, 1 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp salt, 1 can of corn at the very last minute of cooking. THE BEST CHILI I’VE EVER HAD.

To me this recipe is very good when I change the green pepper for a red bell pepper, I add about 8 oz of chipotle peppers in sauce, 1 diced sweet potato (I roasted in the oven for 5 min first after diced), and finally used one fresh jalapeño chopped (with some seeds). The chipotle peppers adds a whole layer of flavor with a hint of sweetness/heat. On each serving I add some shredded sharp cheddar and chopped green onions on top.

Loved this recipe. Wanted to make and didn't have black bean soup on hand, so I used black beans instead. I also did not have chopped tomatoes in puree so used 1 can Rotel Fire Roasted tomatoes w/green chiles and 2 cans no salt added tomato sauce. I did add 2 extra celery stalks, 1 T brown sugar (as suggested by another reviewer), only had a red bell pepper instead of green and 12oz frozen white corn instead of canned corn; and did add 1-1/2 t. cumin and 2 bay leaves. I put in the crockpot for 5 hours on low so the spices and flavors would really blend together. It is delicious!

I had to make some changes from the original, but it’s hard for me not to when using recipes. This recipe is pretty easy, but I have a preference for using certain techniques and adding additional flavor. I first cooked the onions and (Extra) garlic and Iadded some cut up pieces of sun dried tomatoes (maybe a tablespoon or more), and about one inch pieces of dried California and dried ancho chili’s to give it a nice complex and slightly smoky taste to go along with the sweetness, also three fresh tomatoes instead of canned. I also added a little bit of water and later some white northern beans. Otherwise I generally stuck to the recipe, cooking probably atleast 4 hours on the slow cooker setting of my instant pot. Came out delicious- it was meant for making lunches, but everyone ate it for dinner and only two portions left. I’m saving this recipe with my modifications. Thanks!

Loved this recipe. Wanted to make and didn't have black bean soup on hand, so I used black beans instead. I also did not have chopped tomatoes in puree so used 1 can Rotel Fire Roasted tomatoes w/green chiles and 2 cans no salt added tomato sauce. I did add 2 extra celery stalks, 1 T brown sugar (as suggested by another reviewer), only had a red bell pepper instead of green and 12oz frozen white corn instead of canned corn; and did add 1-1/2 t. cumin and 2 bay leaves. I put in the crockpot for 5 hours on low so the spices and flavors would really blend together. It is delicious!

Added Gardein meatless ground beef, caramelized the onions and peppers before adding them to the chili, and cooked it in a pot on medium for an hour instead of a slow cooker. Came out quite tasty and flavorful. If you do it like this, don't forget to stir throughout.

This recipe is a keeper. I just made it this evening and it was very easy to make. Just chop the onions, celery, garlic, and bell peppers and throw everything into the crock pot. The recipe does not call for any salt, and the chili did not need it. It was rich and flavorful without it. It was so rich and satisfying that we did not need a meat side dish for dinner. However, we did top it with grated cheddar cheese to take it over the top, but it is rich enough without the cheese. I highly recommend this recipe!

Too many canned ingredients. This doesn't require a crockpot since everything is mostly cooked that's going in it. A sauce pan on the stove will work just fine. If you're going to make this in a crock pot, start by using dried beans. Also, omit the canned soup and baked beans. Too much sodium and the baked beans will make it too sweet. Garbanzo beans DON'T BELONG IN CHILI!!! Swap them out for kidney beans, geez. Lastly, where is the cumin, coriander and jalapenos.

Good flavour. My mods:
We don't have black bean soup so I did this: 1 can black beans + 2 c. veg broth + 1 heap tbsp of tomato paste + separate 2 tsps corn starch in warm water for thickener. Added all this in as the '1 can Black Bean Soup' that is called for.
Afterwards, some family added a bit more heat but all liked it. Next time I am going to add a bit more chili powder and more peppers - maybe a red pepper.
Everyone loved it ... even the non-vegetarians
Easy and tasty
I would switch out the baked beans for another can of kidney beans just as a personal preference.
As others said it was too sweet for chili and also bland with the season. Won't make thos again.

I made this but omitted the baked beans. I thought it was odd to begin with but after reading others comment, I omitted. I added in place a can of white beans. I also added a can of pinto beans. I added an additional can of mexican corn to the regular corn. I really liked it. We are having the left overs tonight. I gave some to my daughter and she was hesitant since it was vegatarian. But she liked it! She really liked it!
Sodium is way too high
Made this for my daughter that is a vegetarian, she loves it, and the carnivores love it.

I thought this chili was too sweet and otherwise, was lacking flavor. The sweetness likely came from the vegetarian baked beans and the canned corn. I added some cayenne and black pepper to the leftovers to liven it up a bit. I doubt I would make this again.
This was good, but I wouldn't really call it "chili."
